crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Routing Across Automated Market Makers
children.blurb: Routing across automated market makers covers the process of finding and executing a trade through one or more on-chain liquidity pools to achieve the best available outcome.

children.name: Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Yield strategies in smart contracts are automated programs that move deposited capital across decentralised finance protocols to earn returns from lending, liquidity provision, staking, and arbitrage.

children.name: On-Chain Forensics
children.blurb: On-chain forensics is the practice of examining blockchain transaction records to trace the movement of digital assets, attribute addresses to real-world entities, and reconstruct financial activity across crypto markets and decentralised finance protocols.

children.name: Stablecoin Stress Testing
children.blurb: Stablecoin stress testing examines how a stablecoin maintains its peg and meets redemptions under adverse market conditions, including runs, collateral devaluation, liquidity freezes, and operational failures.

children.name: Governance Token Outcomes
children.blurb: Governance token outcomes refers to the measurable results of holding and using tokens that confer voting rights in decentralized protocols, including price performance, voting participation, treasury allocation, and protocol changes.

sections.body: Artificial intelligence in this section means software that reads order books, contract code, ledger history, price feeds and voting records, then acts or reports. It is not a single product but a set of methods applied to exchange routing, yield hunting, forensic tracing, stablecoin stress and governance token analysis. The work is live, not theoretical, with models running against real blockchains and real market data. Routing models compare prices and fees across automated market makers before a swap is submitted. Yield models scan smart contracts for return opportunities and risk flags. Forensic models cluster addresses and follow fund movements on public ledgers.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of the field is uneven. Routing and basic forensic clustering are the most mature, because they rely on public data and clear objectives. Yield strategies are less settled, since smart contract risk and temporary loss from price changes are hard to price in advance. Stablecoin stress testing remains largely simulation, with no widely accepted model for a real loss of a stablecoin's peg. Governance token outcomes are the least predictable, because voting behaviour is sparse and easily manipulated. The honest limit is that these models describe patterns, they do not guarantee future returns or safety. The site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, but that count is a snapshot of market interest, not a measure of reliability.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Routing Across Automated Market Makers explains how a model chooses among pools and fee tiers, and a reader would start there for the mechanics of trade execution. Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts covers how models search for lending, staking and liquidity provision returns, and it pairs naturally with the routing page because both depend on fee and price data. On-Chain Forensics describes how address clustering and flow tracing work, and it is the page to consult when the question is who moved funds, not how to earn. Stablecoin Stress Testing shows how simulations of redemptions and collateral shocks are built, and it connects to forensics because both rely on ledger history. Governance Token Outcomes examines how voting power and proposal results are modelled, and it is the least technical of the five, focused on incentives rather than execution.
